info.title: bevy-ts Remote Protocol
info.description: Methods bevy-ts serves next to stock bevy_remote. One contract for every bevy-ts crate: each method names its owning crate in x-bevy-ts-crate and is served only when that crate's plugin is added. Adding a method or field is a minor bump; removing, renaming or retyping anything is a major bump. Methods with x-bevy-ts-channel are not HTTP methods: they are JSON-RPC notifications on a viewport's Mach channel, sent by the side it names (both: each side sends it).

methods.name: bevy-ts/hello
methods.summary: Handshake: protocol, bevy-ts, Bevy and JS engine versions, entry, generation, dev features, and the engine build with its exposed Rust sets and exported params.

methods.name: bevy-ts/discover
methods.summary: The OpenRPC document this server was built with.

methods.name: bevy-ts/reload
methods.summary: Recompiles from disk and applies the result (dev only).

methods.name: bevy-ts/reload+watch
methods.summary: One message per reload attempt from any cause: compiling, then applied or failed.

methods.name: bevy-ts/schema
methods.summary: One schema per component, TS (live and undeclared) and reflected Rust, in registry.schema's shape.

methods.name: bevy-ts/get_components
methods.summary: world.get_components for TS and reflected components.
methods.description: TS components come from their native layout; reflected ones through bevy_ts::reflect_value::read, in the shape TSX takes (docs/reflection.md): Duration as seconds, Handle<T> as its asset path or null (a script-made asset as its ref { $asset, type }, since 1.30.0), 64- and 128-bit integers past 2^53 as decimal strings, a newtype component as { value }. Since 1.29.0.

methods.name: bevy-ts/get_components+watch
methods.summary: Streams components whose change tick moved since the last message.

methods.name: bevy-ts/mutate_components
methods.summary: Writes one field of a TS or reflected component and marks it changed.
methods.description: For a reflected component, path is a reflection path (empty for the whole component) and the value is written by bevy_ts::reflect_value::write over the default's value at that path, in every form TSX takes; what get_components reads can be sent back as is. A Handle<T> slot also takes a script-made asset's ref { $asset, type } or an asset value { $of, props } (since 1.30.0). A component Bevy computes (GlobalTransform, ComputedNode, TextLayoutInfo) refuses writes. Since 1.29.0.

methods.name: bevy-ts/pause
methods.summary: Stops or resumes every bevy-ts stage and Time<Virtual>; rendering keeps running.

methods.name: bevy-ts/step
methods.summary: While paused, runs that many frames and pauses again.

methods.name: bevy-ts/screenshot
methods.summary: Saves what the run shows as a PNG at path, on the first rendered frame with no render pipeline still compiling and no asset still loading, and answers once the file is written. Works while paused: pause and step to choose the frame. Since 1.32.0.

methods.name: bevy-ts/entities
methods.summary: A snapshot of every entity: id, Name, parent and component names.

methods.name: bevy-ts/entities+watch
methods.summary: The snapshot, then at most one message per frame of structural changes.

methods.name: bevy-ts/systems
methods.summary: TS systems with stage, access, generation, last run time and last error.

methods.name: bevy-ts/log+watch
methods.summary: console.* output and bevy-ts errors and warnings.

methods.name: bevy-ts/tsx_tree
methods.summary: Every scene root with its nodes, in description order (a level's in file order), parents before children: id, entity, key path, element type, source, tombstoned.

methods.name: bevy-ts/tsx_node
methods.summary: One node by entity or id: its source chain, and the components tsx inserted with each field's provenance and last written value.

methods.name: bevy-ts/tsx_find
methods.summary: Every node whose source chain contains a location: one prefab element maps to all its instances, runtime mounts included.

methods.name: bevy-ts/tsx_tree+watch
methods.summary: The tree, then one message per reconcile with what it changed.

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_attach
methods.summary: Makes a viewport for a view (the game, or a preview) and checks in its Mach service; a second attach of a view replaces that view's viewport.

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_detach
methods.summary: Ends the viewport's service and releases its surfaces; the game keeps running.

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_resize
methods.summary: Resizes the virtual window at the next frame boundary.

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_input
methods.summary: Queues viewport input events, as the channel's input messages do.

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_mode
methods.summary: Switches between play and edit; answers the mode in force. A switch from play to edit is a Stop: the world is rebuilt from source before it answers (1.24).

errors.message: A Play was refused: the message is a sentence to show as is, `data` is a ViewportPlayRefused (1.24).
Invalid params, among them `camera: "editor"` in, or entering, Play: "The editor camera is not available in Play." (1.25).

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_mode+watch
methods.summary: The mode on open and on every change, with what changed it (1.24).

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_camera
methods.summary: Gets or sets the editor camera's pose, or a preview viewport's camera.

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_pick
methods.summary: Every hit at a point, nearest first, and what a click there would select.

errors.message: No editor camera, or the game view is in force: "Picking needs the editor camera." (1.25).

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_select
methods.summary: Sets the selection by entities or by source location.

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_selection+watch
methods.summary: The selection on open and on every change.

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_tools
methods.summary: Gets or sets the transform gizmo's mode, space and snap (1.17).

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_tools+watch
methods.summary: The gizmo tools on open and on every change (1.17).

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_edits+watch
methods.summary: Viewport edits: one per gizmo drag on release, and each status change.

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_edit_result
methods.summary: The editor's answer to a tsx edit.

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_revert
methods.summary: Restores an edit's before value.

methods.name: bevy-ts/viewport_stats
methods.summary: Frames, skips, dropped ticks, GPU time and input-to-frame latency.

methods.name: bevy-ts/assets
methods.summary: Every file under the asset root, with kind, loader and load state; loads nothing.

methods.name: bevy-ts/assets+watch
methods.summary: The asset list, then each frame's changes.

methods.name: bevy-ts/asset_thumbnail
methods.summary: A PNG of an asset, rendered offscreen.

methods.name: bevy-ts/asset_preview
methods.summary: Loads a mesh or glTF scene into an isolated preview scene a viewport can attach to.

methods.name: bevy-ts/asset_preview_control
methods.summary: Plays, pauses or switches a preview's glTF animation.

methods.name: bevy-ts/asset_preview_close
methods.summary: Despawns a preview's scene and frees its render layer.

methods.name: bevy-ts/level_list
methods.summary: Open levels: hash, included files, extensions used, diagnostics.

methods.name: bevy-ts/level_open
methods.summary: Opens a .bsn under the asset root as a level root level:<file>, with no TS call: reads it and every file it includes from disk, composes and reconciles before it replies. A failed open opens nothing; an open level answers as it is. Runs no system. Since 1.19.

methods.name: bevy-ts/level_close
methods.summary: Closes an open level: its entities despawn. A closed level stays closed until level_open names it again, whoever opened it. Since 1.19.

methods.name: bevy-ts/level_node
methods.summary: One level-placed entity by entity or name path: its owner chain, its overrides with locations, the scene component it instances.

methods.name: bevy-ts/level_catalog
methods.summary: The scene components of the running generation a level can place, with file, line and props (1.12). No watch: it changes only when a TS reload applies.

methods.name: bevy-ts/level_write
methods.summary: A batch of writer operations on one level file, made against a content hash. The disk wins: a moved file is reloaded first, then the batch replays by name path or is a conflict.

methods.name: bevy-ts/level_apply
methods.summary: Moves an override one owner inward: into the next .bsn file in one transaction, or, when that is TSX, hands the editor the edit and the batch that removes the override.

methods.name: bevy-ts/level+watch
methods.summary: Level events: opened, closed, loaded, failed, written, external, rebased, conflict.

methods.name: hello
methods.summary: Viewer to engine on the channel: attach, with the reply port in the message, naming the viewer. Engine to viewer: the answer to each hello, listing the input types the engine reads (1.10).

methods.name: bye
methods.summary: Viewer to engine: detach.

methods.name: replaced
methods.summary: Engine to viewer: a newer hello took the viewport; this viewer is now gone (1.10).

methods.name: input
methods.summary: Viewer to engine: one input event per message.

methods.name: tick
methods.summary: Viewer to engine: one per vsync of the hole's display.

methods.name: resize
methods.summary: Viewer to engine: the hole's size.

methods.name: visible
methods.summary: Viewer to engine: the hole was shown or hidden.

methods.name: focus
methods.summary: Viewer to engine: the hole gained or lost focus.

methods.name: surface
methods.summary: Engine to viewer: an IOSurface of a ring, sent once per slot.

methods.name: frame
methods.summary: Engine to viewer: a slot holds the newest finished frame.

methods.name: cursor
methods.summary: Engine to viewer: the cursor icon.

methods.name: cursor_grab
methods.summary: Engine to viewer: the cursor grab mode.

methods.name: cursor_warp
methods.summary: Engine to viewer: game code moved the cursor (points).

methods.name: ime_area
methods.summary: Engine to viewer: where the composition is (points).

methods.name: ime_allowed
methods.summary: Engine to viewer: whether IME is on.

protocol.description: The protocol version (semver) this server speaks.

engine.description: The JS engine and its version.

entry.description: The entry file, under bevy-ts dev.

build.description: Which engine binary runs: the prebuilt one or a project engine (protocol 1.4).

sets.description: Rust system sets exposed to TS with app.ts_set, by name (protocol 1.4).

params.description: Rust system params exported to TS with app.ts_param (protocol 1.4).

inspector.description: The CDP address when the inspector is on.

hash.description: The project engine's hash of its Rust inputs; prebuilt-<version>-<target> for the prebuilt engine.

name.description: The TS type, such as ReadRapierContext.

standsFor.description: The Bevy spelling the export stands for, such as ResMut<Time<Virtual>>: a TS param written that way is this export (1.27).

names.description: Only these components (type paths, TS names or short paths).

FieldType.description: A field's type. `timer` is Bevy's `Timer` (24 bytes, align 8) and `stopwatch` its `Stopwatch` (16, align 8), each read and written as an object of their fields: a timer's `elapsed`, `duration` (seconds), `times_finished_this_tick`, `mode` (`Once` or `Repeating`), `paused`, `finished`; a stopwatch's `elapsed` and `paused`. Writing a whole one sets every field: a field left out is zero; write one field by its path (`.cooldown.duration`). `string` and `list` are heap fields (protocol 1.33.0), Rust's `String` and `Vec<T>` in the component's own bytes: a JSON string, or an array of the list's item type `of` (a number kind, `bool` or `string`), each written whole by `.field` (`.field[i]` on a list is refused). A component with one starts with an 8-byte header the layout's offsets and `size` include.

declared.description: False for a component the live generation no longer declares; its data stays.

EditorInfo.description: How an editor treats a component: whose it is, whether the engine maintains it, whether Add component may offer it, and its icon category.

ComponentSchema.description: A component's schema in the shape stock registry.schema uses, plus x-bevy-ts for TS components and x-bevy-ts-editor for every component.

path.description: .field, .field.x|y|z|w or .field[i] for TS components; a reflect path for Rust ones.

EntitiesWatchMessage.description: The first message carries `snapshot`; later ones carry one frame's structural changes. A gap in `seq` means resubscribe.

Stage.description: The bevy-ts stage a system runs in (one per Bevy main and fixed schedule), or preStartup, startup, postStartup, onEnter, onExit, onTransition, observer, oneShot (a one-shot system) or schedule (a custom schedule, named in schedule.label) for systems outside them. (1.28) every main and fixed schedule, the startup lists, oneShot and schedule. (1.30) onTransition.

read.description: Components its queries read and never write.

write.description: Components some query of it takes as Mut.

schedule.description: Where it runs: {kind: preStartup|startup|postStartup|stage|schedule|onEnter|onExit|observer|oneShot, ...}; a custom schedule's is {kind: schedule, label} with its label (game::Waves, net:tick).

params.description: Its params as the compile step declared them: kind query, single, populated, removedComponents, systemChangeTick, res, resMut, local, commands, messageReader, messageWriter, state, nextState, on, port or bundle. Query data may hold has, anyOf and ref; filters or and spawned; on lifecycle discard and despawn.

TsxNodeId.description: A tsx node's identity: a hash of its scene root and key path, in hex. Stable across runs and reloads.

TsxProvenance.description: How a field got its value: `controlled` (`f`), `initial` (`initialF`), `default` (neither), `bound` (`f={() => ...}`), `override` (set by a level file).

type.description: The element type that made the node: `entity`, a UI tag, or the outermost prefab.

tombstoned.description: Despawned by something other than tsx; not respawned until a restart or a key change.

level.description: (1.12) Set when a level placed the entity; absent for a TSX-only node.

file.description: The outermost level file (a sidecar's path for a scene overlay).

written.description: Written in that file, rather than coming from a prefab, an included level or the scene's TSX.

missing.description: (1.21) One per placeholder entry on the entity: a component the level writes whose code is missing, failed or does not fit. Absent when there is none.

scene.description: (1.23) True when the component is the entity's own scene component, the one its row instances; absent for a patch component.

root.description: (1.15) The root the node is in.

parent.description: (1.15) The node id of the nearest ancestor row, or null at the root's top. Slot steps (`<Show>`, `<For>`) are in the key path but are not rows.

sidecar.description: (1.12) An app.scene root's sidecar level path, whether or not the file exists.

value.description: The last value tsx wrote (null for a bound field not delivered yet).

source.description: The element that made the entity, then each prefab call site above it, innermost first. The editor picks the frame in the file it has open.

components.description: Components tsx inserted, by element name (`game::Health`, `Transform`, `Name`, `mesh`, `text`).

depth.description: Where in the node's source chain the location matched: 0 is the element itself, 1 the innermost prefab call site, and so on.

TsxTreeWatchMessage.description: The first message carries `snapshot`; later ones carry one reconcile's changes: nodes added, removed, tombstoned, whose source moved, whose values tsx wrote, and sibling lists whose order changed. A client that applies `added` and `removed`, then replaces each `ordered` parent's children with `children`, holds the tree `tsx_tree` returns. A gap in `seq` means resubscribe.

removed.description: Every node gone, its whole subtree included (1.15).

ordered.description: (1.15) Each sibling list that gained a child, lost one or changed order since the last message, with its full order as `tsx_tree` gives it. A list whose parent was removed is not sent.

TsxOrdered.description: One sibling list's full child order.

parent.description: The list's parent row, or null for the root's top.

caps.description: Caps Lock on (1.9). The engine may ignore it.

Modifiers.description: Modifier keys held; absent means up.

x.description: Points from the hole's top left.

dx.description: Raw motion, kept while the cursor is locked.

buttons.description: Buttons held during the event (1.9). The engine may ignore it.

PointerEvent.description: A pointer event in the hole.

WheelEvent.description: Scroll, with precise deltas in pixels or lines.

x.description: Points from the hole's top left (1.9).

phase.description: As WheelEvent.phase (1.9). The engine may ignore it.

cursor.description: UTF-8 byte range in the preedit text.

FocusEvent.description: The hole gained or lost keyboard focus.

VisibleEvent.description: The hole was shown or hidden.

touches.description: Every touch still down after the event. A touch absent that was down has ended (cancelled, on cancel).

t.description: (1.20) When the touch happened, in ms on the viewer device's own clock. Only compared within one stream, where it mostly rises: a move sent late keeps its own time.

id.description: Stable while the touch is down.

x.description: Points from the hole's top left.

buttons.description: In the W3C standard mapping's order; on connected and state.

axes.description: In the W3C standard mapping's order, -1 to 1, y down; on connected and state.

GamepadEvent.description: A gamepad on the viewer's device, W3C Gamepad API standard mapping (1.10). A state is sent only on change.

kind.description: app: abyme.app's surface view; stream: abyme-stream.

device.description: The name of the device that shows the surface.

viewer.description: From the viewer (1.10); absent from an older one.

inputs.description: From the engine (1.10): the input types it reads.

viewer.description: The new viewer's, as its hello gave it; {} when it named none.

ReplacedMessage.description: To the viewer a newer hello replaced (1.10).

ViewportInput.description: One input event from the viewer.

hz.description: The display's refresh, for pacing before the first tick.

service.description: The Mach bootstrap name to look up and say hello on.

viewport.description: The viewport's id for the other viewport methods; the game viewport is 0.

display.description: The display the hole is on (CGDirectDisplayID), when it moves display.

viewport.description: A viewport id from viewport_attach; default the game viewport (0).
A viewport id from viewport_attach; default the game viewport (0).

ViewportCameraChoice.description: Which camera the viewport shows. In edit mode `auto` and `editor` show the editor camera with its tools, `game` the game cameras with the tools off and the world paused. Play always shows the game cameras; `editor` is refused there. `auto` is the default and may grow with a later two-pane view (1.25).

ui.description: Draw the game's UI over the editor view (edit only; default false).

gamepadUnfocused.description: Pass gamepad input while the hole has no focus.

started.description: Whether the game's TS `Startup` systems have run in this world: false under `bevy-ts dev --edit` until the first play or step (1.18). Absent from older engines: treat the game as started.

gameCameras.description: The game cameras Play would turn on: not the editor's or previews', alive, their own active flag on. In Play, the ones on. Under `--edit` before the first Play, only level and scene cameras (1.25). Absent from older engines: unknown. `camera`, the choice in force, is absent there too: treat it as `auto`.

started.description: Whether the game's TS `Startup` systems have run in this world.

gameCameras.description: The game cameras Play would turn on: not the editor's or previews', alive, their own active flag on. In Play, the ones on. Under `--edit` before the first Play, only level and scene cameras (1.25).

ViewportModeWatch.description: `bevy-ts/viewport_mode+watch`'s message: the mode as `viewport_mode` answers it, and its cause (1.24).

ViewportModeCause.description: What sent a mode message: `engine` on open, `client` a `viewport_mode`, `pause` or `step` call, `restart` a `restart` reload, `failed` a refused Play or camera choice (the mode unchanged) (1.24), `cameras` only `gameCameras` changed: a reload, a level edit or a game system added or removed a game camera (1.25).

ViewportPlayRefused.description: The `data` of a refused Play's error (1.24).

reason.description: `no-generation`: no generation has been applied yet; `compile-errors`: the newest compile failed.

frame.description: Frame the selection, or a preview's scene.

viewport.description: A viewport id from viewport_attach; default the game viewport (0).

ViewportSelectParams.description: Entities, or a source location resolved as bevy-ts/tsx_find resolves it.

namePath.description: bsn: the instance's name path in its level.

owners.description: bsn: every level frame that could hold the edit, outermost first.

target.description: bsn: the frame the edit is written to under levels.prefabEdits.

policy.description: bsn: the levels.prefabEdits policy that chose the target.

EditRoute.description: Who may persist an edit to this field: bsn (bevy-ts, levels), tsx (the editor), locked (bound or rejected), transient (ECS only).

node.description: The TSX node id, 16 hex digits as bevy-ts/tsx_node gives it.

snap.description: Drags move, turn or scale in whole steps.

SnapSteps.description: Fixed, as Bevy's editor prototype sets them.

ViewportTools.description: `origin` is who made the last change: `editor` by the method, `viewport` by a key, `engine` before any.

gpuMs.description: Mean GPU time per frame, submit to completion.

gpuAllocatedBytes.description: The GPU device's allocated bytes (Metal currentAllocatedSize), engine-wide.

AssetsWatchMessage.description: The full list first, then the changes of each frame that had any.

png.description: Base64 PNG; null for kinds with no thumbnail.

pending.description: Rendering has started and is not done: ask again. Meshes and glTF scenes render offscreen over a few frames; images answer at once.

icon.description: A CSS cursor name, or hidden.

LevelHash.description: A level file's content hash: FNV-1a of its bytes, 16 hex digits.

LevelExtensionUse.description: A use of a .bsn extension: E1 comments, E2 scene component instances, E3 child overrides, E4 quoted names, U1 negative numbers.

hash.description: The root file's hash as last applied.

files.description: The level and every file it includes.

diagnostics.description: The last load's error and warnings.

LevelOpener.description: Who opened a level: app.level (ts), add_level (rust), bevy-ts/level_open (editor) or a scene's sidecar.

reason.description: failed: invalid (not a .bsn path inside the asset root), not-found, or load (a file fails to parse or resolve).

diagnostics.description: failed: each with its file, line and column where known.

closed.description: False when the level was not open.

owners.description: Every level frame that could hold an edit, outermost first.

source.description: The TSX source chain inside the instance, innermost first.

prefab.description: The scene component the entity instances, if any; still named when it is a placeholder (1.21).

props.description: A scene component instance's @props, beside its fields; empty for anything else. (1.7)

patches.description: (1.12) Components the file adds that the entity's prefab does not give, named as LevelOverride.component names them. (1.23) A placeholder patch component the file writes is listed too, by the name the file writes; the entity's own scene component never is.

missing.description: (1.21) The entity's placeholder entries; absent when there is none.

MissingReason.description: (1.21) Why a level entry is a placeholder: no live code registers the type (`unregistered`), its code threw or the TS build failed (`failed`), or saved fields or props do not fit live code (`mismatch`).

MissingComponent.description: (1.21) A component a level writes whose code is missing, failed or does not fit. Its saved text is kept in the file.

scene.description: (1.23) True when the component is the entity's own scene component, the one it instances; absent for a patch component.

fields.description: Saved fields and props as written, each value its saved text; a prop keeps its `@`. A mismatch lists only the misfits.

expected.description: Where its code was expected: the throw, the file that did not build, or the declaration this process last saw live. Absent when unknown, as after a restart.

misfit.description: mismatch: why each listed field or prop does not fit.

overrides.description: A missing scene component: the entries below it with no base of their own, kept and not spawned.

path.description: The name path below the instance.

LevelValue.description: A value the writer prints: a number (a float), {int}, a bool, a string, {type, lanes} for a vector or {path} for a variant or constant.

LevelOp.description: One writer operation on a name path.

path.description: A name path from the file's top; `#n` is the n-th unnamed sibling.
A name path from the file's top; `#n` is the n-th unnamed sibling.
A name path from the file's top; `#n` is the n-th unnamed sibling.

field.description: A scene component field rather than an @prop.

path.description: A name path from the file's top; `#n` is the n-th unnamed sibling.

field.description: A scene component field rather than an @prop.

parent.description: A name path from the file's top; `#n` is the n-th unnamed sibling.

name.description: Optional (1.12): without it the writer picks the first free sibling name.

include.description: add_instance: a level to include instead.

asset.description: add_entity (1.12): a .glb or .gltf path, written as WorldAssetRoot("path#Scene0"), or a .bsn to include.

path.description: A name path from the file's top; `#n` is the n-th unnamed sibling.
A name path from the file's top; `#n` is the n-th unnamed sibling.
A name path from the file's top; `#n` is the n-th unnamed sibling.

parent.description: A name path from the file's top; `#n` is the n-th unnamed sibling.

index.description: (1.12) The place among the parent's written children; last when absent.

parent.description: A name path from the file's top; `#n` is the n-th unnamed sibling.

path.description: A name path from the file's top; `#n` is the n-th unnamed sibling.

component.description: As LevelOverride.component names it, or any path a .bsn patch resolves.

text.description: The patch as written; the inverse of a remove_component carries it.

path.description: A name path from the file's top; `#n` is the n-th unnamed sibling.

base.description: null (1.12): the file does not exist yet.

reason.description: conflict: `target removed` or `changed on disk`; refused: `not-found`, `prefab-internal`, `exists`, `invalid`, `internal` or `io`; (1.21) `missing`: a set, revert, set_prop or revert_prop on a placeholder component, `unknown`: a write of a type no live code registers.

lines.description: Changed line ranges in the new file, 1-based, inclusive.

disk.description: conflict: the disk's value of the field, as written.

inverse.description: The batch that undoes this one.

created.description: (1.12) One per entity the batch added, in order; entity is null when the level is not open.

field.description: A field of `component`, or `@prop` for a scene prop of the instance's scene component (1.7).

status.description: written: moved to the next .bsn owner inward; tsx: the next owner is TSX, so the editor writes `edit` and, on success, sends `then` with level_write.

target.description: element: set `prop` on the element at `element`; default: rewrite the default of `prop` in the scene's destructuring at `element` (`static scene({ hp = 100 })`). (1.7)

chain.description: The element that sets the field, then each prefab call site above it, innermost first: for following a passed-through prop. (1.7)

level.description: The file the event is about.

id.description: written, rebased, conflict: the batch's id.

diagnostics.description: failed: the errors; loaded (1.21): the level's diagnostics, a `warning:` per placeholder entry among them.

LevelProp.description: One @prop of a scene component instance: its type, the value it takes, and whether the level sets it.

value.description: The level's value, or the scene's default when the level does not set it.

ViewportView.description: What a viewport shows: "game", or a preview from asset_preview.

viewport.description: A viewport id from viewport_attach; default the game viewport (0).
A viewport id from viewport_attach; default the game viewport (0).

path.description: An asset path under the asset root: a mesh or glTF scene.

pending.description: The asset is loading: ask again.

preview.description: The preview id to attach a viewport to with view { preview }; null while pending.

animations.description: The glTF's animation names (or Animation<i> when unnamed), in file order.

animation.description: The animation to switch to, by name.

FrameTimes.description: Over the last 1000: the engine's update time (CPU, engine-wide) and this viewport's frames from submit to GPU completion.

type.description: The prop's type as the manifest writes it ({ "kind": "f32" }).

path.description: An absolute path ending in .png, in a folder that exists.

frame.description: The bevy-ts frame the shot shows.
